classification.difficultyReason: Choose between rationalisation, reciprocal substitution and simplifying both sides to a common expression, preserving the common domain during factor cancellation.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{\tan\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}=\sin\theta\cos\theta$.

Use $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$, then convert to sine and cosine.

$\dfrac{1+\cos\theta}{1-\cos\theta}=(\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta)^2$.

Multiply numerator and denominator by $1+\cos\theta$, then use $1-\cos^2\theta=\sin^2\theta$.

$\dfrac{\sec\theta\operatorname{cosec}\theta}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta-\sin\theta}=\sec^3\theta$.

Write $\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\frac{1}{\sin\theta}$ and simplify the denominator using $1-\sin^2\theta=\cos^2\theta$.

Both sides equal $\sin\theta\cos\theta$.

Convert each side to sine and cosine and use $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$.
answer.worked:
For $\sin\theta\ne0$ and $\cos\theta\ne0$, simplify each side separately.
$$\begin{align*}(\sec\theta-\cos\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta-\sin\theta)&=\frac{1-\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\frac{1-\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta}\\(\sec\theta-\cos\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta-\sin\theta)&=\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\frac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta}\\(\sec\theta-\cos\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta-\sin\theta)&=\sin\theta\cos\theta\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{\tan\theta+\cot\theta}&=\frac{1}{\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}}\\\frac{1}{\tan\theta+\cot\theta}&=\frac{\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}\\\frac{1}{\tan\theta+\cot\theta}&=\sin\theta\cos\theta\end{align*}$$
Both sides equal $\sin\theta\cos\theta$, so the identity is proved.

answer.short:
$(1-\cos\theta)(1+\sec\theta)=\sin\theta\tan\theta$.

Write $\sec\theta=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}$ and use the difference of squares.
answer.worked:
For $\cos\theta\ne0$, write $1+\sec\theta=\dfrac{1+\cos\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and use the difference of squares:
$$\begin{align*}(1-\cos\theta)(1+\sec\theta)&=\frac{(1-\cos\theta)(1+\cos\theta)}{\cos\theta}\\(1-\cos\theta)(1+\sec\theta)&=\frac{1-\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\\(1-\cos\theta)(1+\sec\theta)&=\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\\(1-\cos\theta)(1+\sec\theta)&=\sin\theta\tan\theta\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
Both sides equal $\dfrac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}$.

Rewrite each side in sine and cosine and cancel its common factor.
answer.worked:
For $\sin\theta\ne0$ and $\cos\theta\ne0$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sec\theta-\tan\theta}{\sec\theta+\tan\theta}&=\frac{\frac{1}{\cos\theta}-\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}}{\frac{1}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}}\\\frac{\sec\theta-\tan\theta}{\sec\theta+\tan\theta}&=\frac{(1-\sin\theta)/\cos\theta}{(1+\sin\theta)/\cos\theta}\\\frac{\sec\theta-\tan\theta}{\sec\theta+\tan\theta}&=\frac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\cot\theta-\cos\theta}{\cot\theta+\cos\theta}&=\frac{\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}-\cos\theta}{\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}+\cos\theta}\\\frac{\cot\theta-\cos\theta}{\cot\theta+\cos\theta}&=\frac{\cos\theta(1-\sin\theta)/\sin\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)/\sin\theta}\\\frac{\cot\theta-\cos\theta}{\cot\theta+\cos\theta}&=\frac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}\end{align*}$$
Both sides have the same value, so the identity is proved.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{1+\sin\theta}{1-\sin\theta}=(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)^2$.

Multiply numerator and denominator by $1+\sin\theta$, then use $1-\sin^2\theta=\cos^2\theta$.
